project_description: This project aims to model how environmental fabrication parameters affect the performance of perovskite solar cells. The goal is to derive a physically interpretable formula that describes how temperature, humidity, and solvent partial pressure during spin coating and thermal annealing influence key photovoltaic performance metrics, especially power conversion efficiency.

features.Spin coater: Absolute Humidity [g/m3]: Ambient humidity during spin coating, influencing solvent evaporation and initial film morphology.
features.Spin coater: Temperature [°C]: Temperature during spin coating, affecting crystallization kinetics and solvent dynamics.
features.Spin coater: Solvent Partial Pressure [p: Vapor pressure of solvent during spin coating, modulating solvent evaporation rate and film uniformity.
features.Thermal annealing: Absolute Humidity [g/: Ambient humidity during annealing, controlling perovskite phase transformation and defect formation.
features.Thermal annealing: Temperature [°C]: Annealing temperature, determining crystal growth rate and final film quality.
features.Short circuit current density, Jsc [mA/c: Current output at zero voltage, reflecting photo-generated charge carrier collection efficiency.
features.Open circuit voltage, Voc [V]: Voltage at zero current, representing electronic quality and recombination losses.
features.Fill factor [%]: Ratio of maximum obtainable power to theoretical maximum, indicating overall cell efficiency and resistance losses.
